messages:
Maya (customer): Hey, hitting a weird 403 after we migrated one of our private deployments to the dedicated VPC gateway. Worked fine earlier in the day, now all API calls from our web frontend fail with 403 and the logs show a missing claim.
Sam (support): Thanks for reporting — can you paste the failing curl and the response body?
Maya (customer): Sure. curl -v -H "Cookie: session=eyJhbGci...signed" "https://api.private.example.com/v1/generate"
Response headers: HTTP/2 403
Body: {
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "message": "missing customer_id claim"
}
Sam (support): That message usually means the auth layer didn't preserve the signed cookie or the claim got truncated. Are you behind any LBs between the app and our gateway?
Maya (customer): We use a GCP HTTP(S) LB in front of an internal Nginx then our dedicated gateway in the VPC. We didn't change cookies.
Tess (eng-platform): @Sam, @Jordan FYI — sounds like header/cookie mangling between LB -> Nginx -> gateway. We saw similar truncation on high header-size requests before.
Jordan (eng-infra): Can you run a tcpdump or send the full raw request your backend receives? Need to confirm whether cookie value is intact when it reaches our gateway.
Maya (customer): Attached small dump: cookie value cut in half. Looks like something split at ~2048 bytes. Our signed cookie is ~3KB because it includes multiple claims and an HMAC blob.
Sam (support): Aha. Envoy/istio sometimes drops or splits headers when they exceed configured buffer/window. Also some LBs will fold large cookies across multiple Set-Cookie or split them. If the HMAC is split, verification fails -> missing claim -> 403.
oncall-bot: Incident: header-length-warning — detected header size > 2KB on route private-prod-gw (auto-alert)
Tess (eng-platform): Do you have any proxies that rewrite cookie serialization? Nginx defaults to limiting header size via large_client_header_buffers. GCP LB may also chunk.
Maya (customer): We don't modify cookie, but switching from regional LB to global HTTP(S) last week coincided with the problem.
Jordan (eng-infra): Patch test: try one of two repros — 1) set a shorter cookie (remove non-essential claims), 2) send same cookie but base64-encode the payload to reduce separators. Any quick repro we can run?
Maya (customer): I tried trimming some optional claims and the call succeeded. So it's definitely size-related.
Sam (support): Workaround: reduce cookie size or move claims into a header that we preserve (e.g., X-Redwood-Customer) but headers might also hit limits. Longer-term we need gateway to accept and reassemble large cookies or change serialization.
Tess (eng-platform): On our side, we can update the dedicated gateway's Envoy config to increase `headers_with_underscores_action` and buffer limits: e.g. 
```
http_conn_manager:
  common_http_protocol_options:
    max_headers_count: 2000
    header_key_format:
      proper_case: {}
```
But that'll need a controlled rollout (risk: memory).
Jordan (eng-infra): Also check GCP LB's cookie-chunking behavior. If LB splits Set-Cookie into multiple header lines, downstream might see them as separate cookies. We need to ensure the HMAC verification recombines correctly.
Maya (customer): Can you confirm which component likely caused this for our Dedicated deployment? We want root cause for our change log.
Sam (support): From the repro (success when cookie smaller) + dump (truncated cookie at LB stage) -> primary cause: external LB chunking/limiting cookie header size. Secondary: gateway's strict validation fails instead of recombining.
Tess (eng-platform): Plan: 1) short-term support guide for customers (doc + recommended cookie size limit ~2KB). 2) infra will test increasing Envoy header limits on a canary dedicated pool. 3) longer-term: accept multipart cookies and recombine signed payloads or move claims to a signed JWT header.
Jordan (eng-infra): I'll open a canary change to increase max_headers_count and tune `max_request_headers_kb` on a small dedicated node pool. Need a rollback plan if memory/latency regresses.
Sam (support): In meantime for Maya, recommended quick fixes: a) strip optional claims from cookie at issuer b) switch to a short session cookie + store full claims server-side c) use a bearer Authorization header (short) for backend calls.
Maya (customer): We'll trim non-essential claims and test. Appreciate the clear path.
Tess (eng-platform): @Jordan please post the canary results here once run. Also we'll draft a KB article for support customers migrating LBs.
Jordan (eng-infra): Can do. Running canary tonight — I'll post metrics (latency, memory, error rate) and the exact Envoy diff.
Sam (support): Thanks everyone. Adding tags: #dedicated #vpc #auth #cookie-size. If anything breaks during canary, ping oncall.
Maya (customer): Update: trimmed claims, rollout looks healthy. No 403s after 30m. Thanks! :thumbsup:
Tess (eng-platform): Great. Follow-up action items: doc + canary + consider helper for recombining split cookie pieces in gateway.
Jordan (eng-infra): Posting canary diff here when ready.
Sam (support): Closing initial ticket pending canary outcome. If it resurfaces, we'll escalate to runtime team for a deeper fix.
